relevance.rationale: This is the single highest-value citation gap in the slice, and it is a corpus problem rather than a reading backlog: the document is ALREADY deep-read and load-bearing across three layers of the repo, with no ref() entry anywhere. It is named by bare arXiv id in at least four Lean library files (QOU/Machinery/HeckeTauAssignmentGaugeGate.lean L38-39, HabiroBracketFamily.lean L22-26, HabiroZetaFamily.lean L5/L30-32, HabiroZeta4Bracket.lean L17), in 7 audit docs (2026-06-03-habiro-per-knot-lambda-derivation, 2026-06-09-per-basis-structural-invariants-scoping, 2026-07-26-tau-coherence-orbit-program-and-habiro-bridge — which contains a verified §1.2-1.5 / §4.5-4.6 deep-read addendum — 2026-07-18-ck-odd-fibre-attack-options, 2026-07-11-qbeta-ck-untested-avenues-and-literature, 2026-06-04-h3-h4-jump-literature-import, 2026-07-19-a6-gswz-habiro-archimedean-state), and two probe scripts are named after it (computations/probes/gswz_frobenius_teichmuller_probe.py, gswz_padic_dilog_modp_probe.py). Because there is no ref() key, none of these citations is checkable by validate-refs and no Lean `-- Ref:` can point at it. Content check against the text confirms the corpus's reading: Def 1.1 gives the Frobenius-twisted p-adic re-expansion gluing between the root-of-unity fibres, and §1.5 gives the K_3(K)-graded modules — the exact 'vertical edge' structure the tau-coherence orbit program (bean qou-vegn) is trying to name. I read §1.1-1.5 (Prologue, integrality/congruence experiments, the original Habiro ring, the Habiro ring of K, the K_3-indexed modules) and the abstract's statement of the admissible-series / infinite-Pochhammer origin; that is enough to confirm the identification without re-doing the corpus's own §4.5-4.6 read.

keyResults.statement: An element of the Habiro ring of a number field is a collection of power series f_m(x) in R[zeta_m][[x]], one per root of unity, satisfying a Frobenius-twisted p-adic re-expansion gluing f_m(x + zeta_pm - zeta_m) = (phi_p f_pm)(x).
keyResults.useForFolio: This is the executable form of the 'vertical edges' the tau-assignment gauge gate cites in prose; registering it lets HeckeTauAssignmentGaugeGate.lean carry a real -- Ref: key instead of a bare arXiv id in a docstring.

keyResults.statement: Modules H_{R,xi} over the Habiro ring of K graded by elements xi of K_3(K), with the correction series at each prime determined by a Bloch-group element and the p-adic dilogarithm.
keyResults.useForFolio: The corpus already grades its Habiro-side objects by K_3 / Bloch-group data (conj:borromean-bloch-group-element, def:quantum-bloch-group); this supplies the published statement of that grading rather than the corpus asserting it in audit prose.
